notes: Golden cases mined from the r4 rehearsal (read-only copy of checkpoints.sqlite). Each case rebuilds the real task packet at that gate, swaps in the CURRENT kit's studio snapshot (skills, rubrics, models) and runs the assigned crew role on it. History references (#N) are indexes into the r4 project history. Assertions are machine-checked; soft assertions are reported but never fail a case. June, scene reviewer, has no cases: r4 stopped before keyframes, so there is no ground truth for her yet.

truth.summary: Vera r4 rejected all three adult sheets because the watch 'switches wrists'. Shaz said that was wrong (#157) and picked option 2 (index 1) after the redo (#160). Options 1 and 3 drop the silver chain in the 8 portraits (checked by eye, p9 head-to-head); option 2 is clean.

asserts.why: The 'watch switches wrists' rejection was false (Shaz, #157). Only a failing check making that claim counts.
Option 2 was the clean sheet Shaz picked (#160).
Options 1 and 3 drop the chain in every portrait.
Real minor defect in options 1 and 3.

truth.summary: Option 2 (index 1) has baked-in view and expression labels ('FRONT VIEW', 'NEUTRAL', ...); Shaz rejected it (#145) and picked option 1 (index 0, no text) (#142). Vera r4 passed all 6 checks and missed the labels. Labels confirmed by eye. Under Vera's rule (pass the checks when at least one option is clean, name the defective option and leave it out of the ranking), the right answer is approved with option 1 picked and option 2's labels written out.

asserts.why: Options 1 and 3 are clean; Vera's rule passes the set when at least one option is clean on every criterion.
Option 2 has rendered text labels; Vera must name them in her notes even when the check passes on the clean options.
The labelled sheet must never be the recommendation.
Shaz picked option 1 (#142).

truth.summary: Vera r4 approved all three childhood-room plates. Shaz rejected them: "these backgrounds are all bullshit. this don't look like a pixar film" - empty, generic, undressed rooms (#225).

asserts.why: Shaz rejected every plate (#225).
The failure is the empty, generic, undressed room (style / not dressed from the story), not its palette.
A muted palette alone is never a failure; the defect is the generic, undressed room, not its colours.

asserts.why: Shaz rejected this brief (#225).

truth.summary: Beau authoring the childhood-room brief from scratch (no feedback in the packet). Shaz rejected the r4 v1 brief for calm blank walls and 'few plain unmarked storage objects' and asked for a lived-in room dressed from the story (#225); he approved v2 (#231).

asserts.why: Rule [L-LIGHT-SPEC]: brief ends with a Light line (one key light) and a Palette line (vivid colours, hero accent).
The film accent is never named in brief text.
Rule [L-LAYOUT-REF]: direction includes a layout part in words.
Shaz rejected 'a few plain unmarked storage objects' (#225).
The room must say it is 8-year-old Shaz's (scientist dream, sunglasses).

Locked childhood fact Shaz approved.

truth.summary: Shaz approved script v1 (#8), but its beat 2 "no A/C" was read aloud by TTS as "A slash C" and had to be regenerated as "AC" (#49). Shaz wants that caught at review (Oct 11): Sage must reject the script for the slash abbreviation and must not invent any other defect.

truth.summary: Every location in backgrounds v1 has an empty angles array, and every approved shot in the r4 plan binds angleId null (uses the main background plate). Under the master-plate rule adopted after r4, that configuration is correct, so Sage must APPROVE and must not invent an angles defect. The original r4 expectation (#187) that empty angles should be rejected predates the master-plate rule; Shaz flipped this case on Oct 11.

asserts.why: Every approved shot uses the main plate; empty secondary-angles is correct under the master-plate rule.
Rejecting for empty/missing angles invents a defect: the r4 shot plan needs no secondary angles.

Sage must identify the layout/expression defect.

truth.summary: Pia writes the rev 5 photo-to-sheet prompt for adult Shaz from the real r4 cast state and photo (r4 itself ran rev 4 with Cleo). Checks the P14 sheet rules: hex, fixed eight in order, four views, no vendor words, no child rider on an adult.

asserts.why: [R-SHEET-HEX]: flat #B5B5B5 written as the hex.
[R-SHEET-EIGHT] / Decision 1: the fixed eight in order.
[R-SHEET-VIEWS]: front, three-quarter, profile, back.
Decision 4 and spec 1e: no studio, renderer, T-pose or three-point lighting words.
[C-SKIN-NATURAL]: no skin zoning or nose, ear or cheek colour words (Shaz 2026-10-13, A/B test: zoning caused clown-red).

asserts.pattern: child(like)? proportion|toddler|short legs|long torso|oversized head|enlarged head|larger head
asserts.why: [C-CHILD-RIDER]: children only, never on adults.

truth.summary: Pia writes the rev 5 photo-to-sheet prompt for Shaz at 8 from the real r4 cast state and photo. Same P14 sheet rules, plus the child rider and child heads-tall.

asserts.why: [R-SHEET-HEX]: flat #B5B5B5 written as the hex.

[C-SKIN-NATURAL]: no skin zoning or nose, ear or cheek colour words (Shaz 2026-10-13, A/B test: zoning caused clown-red).

asserts.pattern: slim child build|narrow child shoulders|enlarged expressive head|child proportion
